version.changelog: Fix safety and portability issues: remove hardcoded /Users/yao paths, default to user home, add automatic openclaw.json backup, replace surprising USER.md defaults with neutral placeholders, clarify browser-based Telegram group flow, and document exact openclaw.json fields modified.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: create-agent-with-telegram-group
Version: 0.1.1

The skill is classified as suspicious due to its high-privilege actions and a significant security vulnerability in its design. Specifically, the `SKILL.md` instructions (Workflow Step 7) direct the agent to copy `auth.json` and `models.json` from a 'main' agent to the newly provisioned agent's directory. This action can propagate sensitive credentials and API keys, potentially leading to over-privileged agents. While the bundled Python scripts (`scripts/init_workspace.py`, `scripts/provision_config.py`) are well-defined and perform their stated functions (modifying `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, creating workspace files), the overall scope includes powerful capabilities like modifying core OpenClaw configuration, restarting the gateway, and using browser automation for Telegram group creation. The `SKILL.md` also demonstrates the agent's ability to execute inline Python commands, which, while benign in this instance (model discovery), highlights a potential prompt injection surface.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with its stated purpose: it provisions an OpenClaw agent, edits the user's ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, and creates a workspace and Telegram binding; included scripts are readable and do what the docs describe.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the behavior: scripts and SKILL.md focus on creating a workspace, editing ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, and binding a Telegram group. No unrelated credentials or external services are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions explicitly read and modify ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and create ~/claw-<agent>. That is appropriate for provisioning. Two minor mismatches to be aware of: (1) SKILL.md says to ensure auth/models files are present (copy from main) but the included scripts do not implement copying of auth-profiles.json/auth.json/models.json; (2) SKILL.md recommends browser automation for Telegram group creation but no automation code is included, so the agent must either orchestrate a separate automation tool or fall back to manual steps as described.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with two small, readable Python scripts and no install spec. No downloads or archive extraction; nothing writes outside the user's home area other than the intended openclaw config and workspace directories.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are requested. The skill reads and writes the user's OpenClaw config (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json) and may require manual access to Telegram via a browser account. Because openclaw.json can contain auth information, users should be aware the skill will read/modify a file that may contain sensitive tokens.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not attempt to persist itself beyond normal files it manages. It only edits the user's OpenClaw config and creates workspaces; it does not alter other skills' configuration or system-wide settings beyond gateway.reload.mode defaulting to 'hybrid' if absent.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims: it edits ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, creates ~/claw-<agent-name>, and helps bind a Telegram group. Before running it: (1) review the two included Python scripts (they are short and readable); (2) backup ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json yourself in case you want a known restore point (the script writes a timestamped backup by default); (3) confirm the chat_id you will pass is correct—mistakes will be written into your config; (4) be aware openclaw.json may contain auth tokens or model profiles—inspect contents first if you have sensitive entries; (5) note that Telegram group creation relies on browser automation or manual steps—no automation code is bundled to create groups automatically; and (6) if you expect the skill to copy auth-profiles.json/auth.json/models.json into the new agent, realize the provided scripts do not perform that copy (you must do it manually or extend the scripts). These points are normal operational cautions rather than indicators of malicious behavior.
